# Build and publish the book

## Build locally

Bookdown compiles the `.Rmd` files and CSS into a GitBook-style website. Building the book does not run the IOBRpy analyses.

Install the R packages once:

```r
install.packages(c("bookdown", "rmarkdown", "knitr"))
```

From the repository root:

```bash
Rscript render_book.R
```

The website is written to `_book/`, with `_book/index.html` as the entry page.

## Pandoc on Windows

RStudio includes Pandoc, but command-line R may not discover it automatically. In PowerShell:

```powershell
$env:RSTUDIO_PANDOC = "C:\Program Files\RStudio\resources\app\bin\quarto\bin\tools"
& "C:\Program Files\R\R-4.3.3\bin\Rscript.exe" "render_book.R"
```

Replace the R and RStudio paths with the installed versions.

If R reports that `htmltools` is too old, install the current package into the project-local library:

```powershell
& "C:\Program Files\R\R-4.3.3\bin\Rscript.exe" -e `
  "dir.create('.r-library', recursive=TRUE, showWarnings=FALSE); install.packages('htmltools', lib='.r-library', repos='https://cloud.r-project.org')"
```

## Preview locally

```bash
python -m http.server 8000 --directory _book
```

Open `http://localhost:8000/`.

## GitHub Pages

Every push to `main` runs `.github/workflows/pages.yml`, renders the book, and deploys:

```text
https://hhn0527.github.io/IOBRpy_book/
```

Chapter order is controlled by `rmd_files` in `_bookdown.yml`. Rebuild locally before pushing and check navigation, code blocks, links, and the author line.
